overview: This Senate resolution names August 7, 2026, National Lighthouse Day, marking the 237th anniversary of the Lighthouse Act of 1789, a law signed by George Washington that made the federal government responsible for lighthouses and was the nation's first public works law. It honors the keepers and their families, including many women, who tended lights through storms and isolation, and notes that many historic lighthouses still face erosion and decay after being automated. The resolution encourages opening lighthouse grounds to the public where possible, asks Americans to mark the day by visiting sites and supporting preservation groups, and restates the Senate's support for preserving historic lighthouses. It does not change any law or provide money. The Senate approved it on August 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say the day draws attention to historic landmarks at risk of decay and honors the people who kept ships safe for generations, while boosting tourism in coastal towns.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, so it does nothing directly to fund the repairs it says many lighthouses need.
